🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Antimicrobial overuse could make common infections harder to treat: Health ministry official

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 06:19:39 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: World AMR Awareness Week is observed from November 18 to 24 every year to improve awareness and understanding of antimicrobial resistance and promote best practices among the public, policymakers and One Health stakeholders

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Misuse and overuse of antimicrobials could undermine decades of medical progress and make even common infections increasingly difficult to treat, a senior health ministry official said on Wednesday, calling for collective action to contain antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Addressing the national observance of World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week 2026 virtually, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava described AMR as one of the most serious public health challenges and stressed the need for a coordinated "One Health" approach to tackle it. This year's theme is "One Health, One Action: Prevent AMR Now". She said medicines that have saved countless lives are gradually losing their effectiveness due to misuse and overuse. Srivastava highlighted the interconnectedness of human and animal health, plant and food systems and the environment, noting that improper use of antimicrobials across these sectors contributes to the emergence and spread of resistance. She said the government has accorded high priority to containing AMR, with the National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance 2.0 (NAP AMR 2.0), 2025-2029, providing a framework for surveillance, infection prevention, responsible antimicrobial use, research and coordinated action. The health ministry's National Programme on AMR Containment, coordinated by the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), focuses on strengthening laboratory capacity for AMR surveillance, infection prevention and control, antimicrobial stewardship and awareness generation, she said. Srivastava urged healthcare professionals to prescribe antibiotics only when clinically indicated and in accordance with treatment guidelines. She also asked pharmacists to ensure appropriate dispensing against valid prescriptions and counsel patients on their correct use. She also advised people against self-medication, sharing antibiotics or using leftover medicines, stressing that antibiotics are not effective against viral infections such as the common cold and influenza.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: More than half of antimicrobial sales in India take place without prescriptions, while nearly half of outpatient antibiotic prescriptions are inappropriate, participants at the event noted.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: World AMR Awareness Week is observed from November 18 to 24 every year to improve awareness and understanding of antimicrobial resistance and promote best practices among the public, policymakers and One Health stakeholders
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Misuse and overuse of antimicrobials could undermine decades of medical progress and make even common infections increasingly difficult to treat, a senior health ministry official said on Wednesday, calling for collective action to contain antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Addressing the national observance of World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week 2026 virtually, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava described AMR as one of the most serious public health challenges and stressed the need for a coordinated "One Health" approach to tackle it. This year's theme is "One Health, One Action: Prevent AMR Now". She said medicines that have saved countless lives are gradually losing their effectiveness due to misuse and overuse. Srivastava highlighted the interconnectedness of human and animal health, plant and food systems and the environment, noting that improper use of antimicrobials across these sectors contributes to the emergence and spread of resistance. She said the government has accorded high priority to containing AMR, with the National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance 2.0 (NAP AMR 2.0), 2025-2029, providing a framework for surveillance, infection prevention, responsible antimicrobial use, research and coordinated action. The health ministry's National Programme on AMR Containment, coordinated by the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), focuses on strengthening laboratory capacity for AMR surveillance, infection prevention and control, antimicrobial stewardship and awareness generation, she said. Srivastava urged healthcare professionals to prescribe antibiotics only when clinically indicated and in accordance with treatment guidelines. She also asked pharmacists to ensure appropriate dispensing against valid prescriptions and counsel patients on their correct use. She also advised people against self-medication, sharing antibiotics or using leftover medicines, stressing that antibiotics are not effective against viral infections such as the common cold and influenza.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: More than half of antimicrobial sales in India take place without prescriptions, while nearly half of outpatient antibiotic prescriptions are inappropriate, participants at the event noted.

articles.title: England launches world's largest AI-aided breast cancer screening trial
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to opt out

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: England's state-run health service said Monday it has launched the world's largest AI-assisted breast cancer screening trial, which is set to involve nearly 700,000 women over the next three years. The National Health Service (NHS) hailed the new trial as having the potential to transform breast cancer diagnosis, as it announced hundreds of women had been invited to take part at the outset. The £10 million ($13 million) programme will assess if tools assisted by artificial intelligence can help improve early cancer detection in screening, which health officials hope will then free up specialist clinicians' time. The AI-assisted reading tool will assist clinicians in reviewing images collected from routine mammograms, according to the NHS. "This is the biggest AI breast cancer trial in the world," Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said in a statement, lauding the tech's "huge potential" while pledging "proper safeguards" to ensure safety and effectiveness. "If successful, this technology could help women get a breast cancer diagnosis and start treatment much more quickly, giving them the best possible chance of recovery." The trial is being led by the University of Warwick, the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, working closely with NHS England. Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to opt out. The NHS stressed screening appointments will proceed as normal, but the AI-assisted tool will be used alongside specialists checking the images to look for cancers that are too small to see or feel.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The trial will test whether AI-assisted tools could allow most images to be reviewed by only one specialist, rather than the current two.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to opt out
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: England's state-run health service said Monday it has launched the world's largest AI-assisted breast cancer screening trial, which is set to involve nearly 700,000 women over the next three years. The National Health Service (NHS) hailed the new trial as having the potential to transform breast cancer diagnosis, as it announced hundreds of women had been invited to take part at the outset. The £10 million ($13 million) programme will assess if tools assisted by artificial intelligence can help improve early cancer detection in screening, which health officials hope will then free up specialist clinicians' time. The AI-assisted reading tool will assist clinicians in reviewing images collected from routine mammograms, according to the NHS. "This is the biggest AI breast cancer trial in the world," Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said in a statement, lauding the tech's "huge potential" while pledging "proper safeguards" to ensure safety and effectiveness. "If successful, this technology could help women get a breast cancer diagnosis and start treatment much more quickly, giving them the best possible chance of recovery." The trial is being led by the University of Warwick, the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, working closely with NHS England. Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to opt out. The NHS stressed screening appointments will proceed as normal, but the AI-assisted tool will be used alongside specialists checking the images to look for cancers that are too small to see or feel.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The trial will test whether AI-assisted tools could allow most images to be reviewed by only one specialist, rather than the current two.

articles.title: Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Jensen Huang’s return

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Wall Street’s main indexes rallied sharply on Monday (November 23, 2026), led by a ​nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks ⁠after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Mr. Huang’s return. Mr. Huang resigned ‌as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and ‌its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling. “Huang’s return ‌marks ⁠one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so ⁠much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive,” said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation. “Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw.” The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion ​in market value on Monday (November 23). The Nasdaq ‌Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Mr. Trump paused his “Liberation Day” tariff package in April 2025. Chip stocks gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing ​between 5.8% and 12.4%.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #13 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 11:45:34 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Jensen Huang’s return

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Wall Street’s main indexes rallied sharply on Monday (November 23, 2026), led by a ​nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks ⁠after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Mr. Huang’s return. Mr. Huang resigned ‌as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and ‌its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling. “Huang’s return ‌marks ⁠one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so ⁠much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive,” said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation. “Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw.” The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion ​in market value on Monday (November 23). The Nasdaq ‌Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Mr. Trump paused his “Liberation Day” tariff package in April 2025. Chip stocks gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing ​between 5.8% and 12.4%.

articles.title: Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 years as recent measures take effect, Petroleum Ministry says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: In a note accessed by The Hindu, the Ministry has said that the oil and gas industry has a long gestation period and so exploration and finance decisions taken more than a decade ago are affecting the industry now

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The government expects domestic oil and gas production to pick up in the next 4-5 years as several steps taken in the recent past begin to bear fruit in an industry typically characterised by long gestation periods, The Hindu has learnt. According to an analysis by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, the current contraction in domestic oil and gas production is due to factors that took place more than a decade ago. However, since then, the government has taken steps such as increasing drilling and exploration to record levels, changing laws and rules to provide stable terms to explorers, and opening new avenues for exploration. “The steps taken in the last few years — new acreage, record drilling, deepwater wells and the revival of Mumbai High — will start showing up in production over the next three to four years,” the note asserted. “That is the nature of this sector: the decisions of one decade decide the output of the next.” The note also argues that now, unlike earlier, the profits of oil and gas companies upstream companies like ONGC and Oil India are being used to fund exploration rather than subsidies. “Until 2015, ONGC and Oil India were made to fund a large share of the subsidy on diesel, LPG and kerosene, through discounts on the crude they sold to oil marketing companies,” the note said. According to data with the Ministry, ONGC paid ₹49,421 crore towards this subsidy in 2012-13 against a profit of ₹20,926 crore, and in 2013-14 paid ₹56,384 crore towards this subsidy against a net profit of ₹22,095 crore. “In both years ONGC gave away more than twice what it earned,” the note said. “Money that should have gone into finding new oil and gas went into keeping retail prices down. This burden was ended from 2015-16. ONGC now keeps its earnings and has sharply raised its spending on exploration.” According to the latest data on the Index of Core Industries, the oil and gas sectors have contracted continuously for 22 and 28 months, respectively.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “In this sector it takes five to ten years to go from awarding a block to first production,” a note prepared by the Ministry and accessed by The Hindu said. “Output in 2026 is the result of what was, and was not, done a decade ago.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #15 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 years as recent measures take effect, Petroleum Ministry says

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 08:32:08 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: In a note accessed by The Hindu, the Ministry has said that the oil and gas industry has a long gestation period and so exploration and finance decisions taken more than a decade ago are affecting the industry now

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The government expects domestic oil and gas production to pick up in the next 4-5 years as several steps taken in the recent past begin to bear fruit in an industry typically characterised by long gestation periods, The Hindu has learnt. According to an analysis by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, the current contraction in domestic oil and gas production is due to factors that took place more than a decade ago. However, since then, the government has taken steps such as increasing drilling and exploration to record levels, changing laws and rules to provide stable terms to explorers, and opening new avenues for exploration. “The steps taken in the last few years — new acreage, record drilling, deepwater wells and the revival of Mumbai High — will start showing up in production over the next three to four years,” the note asserted. “That is the nature of this sector: the decisions of one decade decide the output of the next.” The note also argues that now, unlike earlier, the profits of oil and gas companies upstream companies like ONGC and Oil India are being used to fund exploration rather than subsidies. “Until 2015, ONGC and Oil India were made to fund a large share of the subsidy on diesel, LPG and kerosene, through discounts on the crude they sold to oil marketing companies,” the note said. According to data with the Ministry, ONGC paid ₹49,421 crore towards this subsidy in 2012-13 against a profit of ₹20,926 crore, and in 2013-14 paid ₹56,384 crore towards this subsidy against a net profit of ₹22,095 crore. “In both years ONGC gave away more than twice what it earned,” the note said. “Money that should have gone into finding new oil and gas went into keeping retail prices down. This burden was ended from 2015-16. ONGC now keeps its earnings and has sharply raised its spending on exploration.” According to the latest data on the Index of Core Industries, the oil and gas sectors have contracted continuously for 22 and 28 months, respectively.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “In this sector it takes five to ten years to go from awarding a block to first production,” a note prepared by the Ministry and accessed by The Hindu said. “Output in 2026 is the result of what was, and was not, done a decade ago.

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Production (Noun)
उत्पादन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Production' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Gestation (Noun)
गर्भधारण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Gestation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 📈 Economic, Banking & Finance passage on "Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 years as recent measures take effect, Petroleum Ministry says", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. In a note accessed by The Hindu, the Ministry has said that the oil and gas industry has a long gestation period and so exploration and finance...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 years a' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 year' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 year' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "In a note accessed by The Hindu, the Ministry has said that the oil and gas industry has a long gestation period and so exploration and finance..." (Hinglish Arth: द हिंदू द्वारा प्राप्त एक नोट में, मंत्रालय ने कहा है कि तेल और गैस उद्योग की विकास अवधि लंबी है और इसलिए एक दशक से अधिक पहले लिए गए अन्वेषण और वित्त निर्णय अब उद्योग को प्रभावित कर रहे हैं।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 years as recent measures take effect, Petroleum Ministry says"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. “Output in 2026 is the result of what was, and was not, done a decade ago.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "“Output in 2026 is the result of what was, and was not, done a decade ago." (Hinglish Arth: “2026 में आउटपुट एक दशक पहले जो किया गया था और जो नहीं किया गया था उसका परिणाम है।)

articles.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after U.S. government input
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision”

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nvidia on Monday (November 23, 2026) reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after input from senior U.S. government officials left its board confident he posed no national security risk, less than two weeks after the co-founder resigned due to an alleged spy scandal. U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision.” The board voted unanimously to bring Mr. Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead”, the company said in a statement. Nvidia did not name the government officials it consulted or say what they told the board. The decision came three days after Mr. Trump publicly urged Nvidia to take Mr. Huang back, calling him “one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world” and saying he would “love to see Jensen be given a second chance.” Mr. Trump described Mr. Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions" and said the company should rehire him “if they were smart". Mr. Huang had offered to return, but the board initially refused. Board chair Harvey Jones had said on an earnings call last week that directors had unanimously accepted his resignation and did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO". “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Mr. Huang said, thanking the board, staff, shareholders and his family. “I can’t wait to get back to work.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Huang, 63, stepped down on November 12 following reports that he had a relationship with Alice Huang — no relation — a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company that bought billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips.

1. Core Context & Background: U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision”

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nvidia on Monday (November 23, 2026) reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after input from senior U.S. government officials left its board confident he posed no national security risk, less than two weeks after the co-founder resigned due to an alleged spy scandal. U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision.” The board voted unanimously to bring Mr. Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead”, the company said in a statement. Nvidia did not name the government officials it consulted or say what they told the board. The decision came three days after Mr. Trump publicly urged Nvidia to take Mr. Huang back, calling him “one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world” and saying he would “love to see Jensen be given a second chance.” Mr. Trump described Mr. Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions" and said the company should rehire him “if they were smart". Mr. Huang had offered to return, but the board initially refused. Board chair Harvey Jones had said on an earnings call last week that directors had unanimously accepted his resignation and did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO". “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Mr. Huang said, thanking the board, staff, shareholders and his family. “I can’t wait to get back to work.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Huang, 63, stepped down on November 12 following reports that he had a relationship with Alice Huang — no relation — a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company that bought billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #22 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after U.S. government input

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 11:45:03 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision”

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nvidia on Monday (November 23, 2026) reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after input from senior U.S. government officials left its board confident he posed no national security risk, less than two weeks after the co-founder resigned due to an alleged spy scandal. U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision.” The board voted unanimously to bring Mr. Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead”, the company said in a statement. Nvidia did not name the government officials it consulted or say what they told the board. The decision came three days after Mr. Trump publicly urged Nvidia to take Mr. Huang back, calling him “one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world” and saying he would “love to see Jensen be given a second chance.” Mr. Trump described Mr. Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions" and said the company should rehire him “if they were smart". Mr. Huang had offered to return, but the board initially refused. Board chair Harvey Jones had said on an earnings call last week that directors had unanimously accepted his resignation and did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO". “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Mr. Huang said, thanking the board, staff, shareholders and his family. “I can’t wait to get back to work.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Huang, 63, stepped down on November 12 following reports that he had a relationship with Alice Huang — no relation — a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company that bought billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips.

articles.title: Will use 'all available means' to counter U.S. blockade: Iran
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: War broke out between Iran and the United States on February 28 when U.S.-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Iran said on Monday (November 23, 2026) it would use all means at its disposal to counter a U.S. naval blockade that was imposed in retaliation for its own push to block the Strait of Hormuz. "We will certainly not tolerate these actions and will use all available means to counter U.S. aggression," said Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei in a weekly press briefing. War broke out between Iran and the United States on February 28 when U.S.-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. The conflict has since expanded after Iran retaliated with missile and drone strikes across the region, and with militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entering the fray. The Strait of Hormuz has become the focus of the conflict, with Iran continuing in its efforts to blockade the waterway, vital to global energy supplies. In response, the U.S. imposed its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. It later announced a raft of economic sanctions, and launched a task force to disrupt land routes into Iran. "You should bear in mind that what the Americans have described as economic sanctions, an economic blockade and a naval blockade undoubtedly constitutes an act of military aggression against Iran," said Mr. Baqaei. "Under these circumstances, Iran is entitled, pursuant to Article 51 of the UN Charter, to use any means at its disposal to defend itself." Iranian forces have made multiple announcements in recent weeks of ships catching fire attempting to use routes that Tehran considers off-limits.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Diplomatic efforts to resolve the crisis remain stalled, especially since the collapse of a June deal that laid out a pathway to a permanent settlement.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Will use 'all available means' to counter U.S. blockade: Iran

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 10:48:26 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: War broke out between Iran and the United States on February 28 when U.S.-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Iran said on Monday (November 23, 2026) it would use all means at its disposal to counter a U.S. naval blockade that was imposed in retaliation for its own push to block the Strait of Hormuz. "We will certainly not tolerate these actions and will use all available means to counter U.S. aggression," said Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei in a weekly press briefing. War broke out between Iran and the United States on February 28 when U.S.-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. The conflict has since expanded after Iran retaliated with missile and drone strikes across the region, and with militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entering the fray. The Strait of Hormuz has become the focus of the conflict, with Iran continuing in its efforts to blockade the waterway, vital to global energy supplies. In response, the U.S. imposed its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. It later announced a raft of economic sanctions, and launched a task force to disrupt land routes into Iran. "You should bear in mind that what the Americans have described as economic sanctions, an economic blockade and a naval blockade undoubtedly constitutes an act of military aggression against Iran," said Mr. Baqaei. "Under these circumstances, Iran is entitled, pursuant to Article 51 of the UN Charter, to use any means at its disposal to defend itself." Iranian forces have made multiple announcements in recent weeks of ships catching fire attempting to use routes that Tehran considers off-limits.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Diplomatic efforts to resolve the crisis remain stalled, especially since the collapse of a June deal that laid out a pathway to a permanent settlement.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Iran said on Monday (November 23, 2026) it would use all means at its disposal to counter a U.S. naval blockade that was imposed in retaliation for its own push to block the Strait of Hormuz. "We will certainly not tolerate these actions and will use all available means to counter U.S. aggression," said Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei in a weekly press briefing. War broke out between Iran and the United States on February 28 when U.S.-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. The conflict has since expanded after Iran retaliated with missile and drone strikes across the region, and with militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entering the fray. In response, the U.S. imposed its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. It later announced a raft of economic sanctions, and launched a task force to disrupt land routes into Iran. "You should bear in mind that what the Americans have described as economic sanctions, an economic blockade and a naval blockade undoubtedly constitutes an act of military aggression against Iran," said Mr. Baqaei. "Under these circumstances, Iran is entitled, pursuant to Article 51 of the UN Charter, to use any means at its disposal to defend itself." Iranian forces have made multiple announcements in recent weeks of ships catching fire attempting to use routes that Tehran considers off-limits.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Mapping exercise covers 4.3 lakh square km; focus now on prevention, preparedness, risk reduction, says Science Minister; calls for interdisciplinary research, continuous monitoring to minimise impact

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India has completed a national landslide susceptibility mapping exercise across approximately 4.3 lakh square kilometres, while the landslide inventory database has compiled information on nearly 91,000 historical landslides by the end of 2025, Minister for Science and Technology Jitendra Singh said on Monday (November 23, 2026). He noted that India is progressively shifting its approach to landslide management, from post-disaster relief to prevention, preparedness, and risk reduction, marking a “major transformation” in the country’s disaster management strategy. He was speaking at the 7th World Landslide Forum being held at the Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Faridabad. This is the first time the periodic International Consortium on Landslides and the International Programme on Landslides is being held in India. The 4-day programme brought together international experts, scientists, and policymakers from more than 75 countries. Recalling major landslide disasters in Kerala’s Wayanad and Uttarakhand’s Chamoli, as well as in Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, and Jammu and Kashmir, Dr. Singh stressed the need for interdisciplinary research, continuous monitoring, and coordinated scientific efforts to minimise the impact of such disasters.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The National Landslide Forecasting Centre was established in Kolkata in 2024 and has now extended its activities to 20 districts, according to a statement from the Department of Science and Technology. The Regional Landslide Forecasting System, established in 2020, is supporting experimental and operational forecasting across vulnerable regions, it added.

articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: Mapping exercise covers 4.3 lakh square km; focus now on prevention, preparedness, risk reduction, says Science Minister; calls for interdisciplinary research, continuous monitoring to minimise impact
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Mapping exercise covers 4.3 lakh square km; focus now on prevention, preparedness, risk reduction, says Science Minister; calls for interdisciplinary research, continuous monitoring to minimise impact
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India has completed a national landslide susceptibility mapping exercise across approximately 4.3 lakh square kilometres, while the landslide inventory database has compiled information on nearly 91,000 historical landslides by the end of 2025, Minister for Science and Technology Jitendra Singh said on Monday (November 23, 2026). He noted that India is progressively shifting its approach to landslide management, from post-disaster relief to prevention, preparedness, and risk reduction, marking a “major transformation” in the country’s disaster management strategy. He was speaking at the 7th World Landslide Forum being held at the Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Faridabad. This is the first time the periodic International Consortium on Landslides and the International Programme on Landslides is being held in India. The 4-day programme brought together international experts, scientists, and policymakers from more than 75 countries. Recalling major landslide disasters in Kerala’s Wayanad and Uttarakhand’s Chamoli, as well as in Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, and Jammu and Kashmir, Dr. Singh stressed the need for interdisciplinary research, continuous monitoring, and coordinated scientific efforts to minimise the impact of such disasters.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The National Landslide Forecasting Centre was established in Kolkata in 2024 and has now extended its activities to 20 districts, according to a statement from the Department of Science and Technology. The Regional Landslide Forecasting System, established in 2020, is supporting experimental and operational forecasting across vulnerable regions, it added.

articles.title: Severe anaemia affects less than 2% of population: ICMR survey
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: SAMPADA covered more than 2 lakh individuals from over 81,000 households across 183 districts in 35 States and Union Territories

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: According to a survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), severe anaemia was observed in less than 2% of people in the majority of age groups. The Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA) 2023-2025 was released on Monday (November 23, 2026). It showed that children aged 12-59 months had 42% anaemia prevalence, adolescent girls aged 10-19 years had anaemia prevalence of 46%, adolescent boys aged 10-19 years and men aged 20–59 years had 22-23% anaemia prevalence, whereas women of reproductive age had 56% prevalence. The survey also found that mild anaemia constitutes a substantial proportion of the overall anaemia burden. “SAMPADA provides nationally representative estimates of anaemia across children, adolescents, adults, pregnant and lactating women and older adults, together with detailed information on micronutrient deficiencies to evaluate potential causes of anaemia. It is encouraging that prevalence of anaemia is lower in SAMPADA compared to previous national surveys. The comprehensive anaemia profiling in the SAMPADA survey provides an evidence base to strengthen the ongoing national efforts towards Anaemia Mukt Bharat,” said Rajiv Bahl, secretary, Department of Health Research. The report noted that about half of anaemic women, including pregnant and lactating women, adolescent girls, and children, have mild anaemia, indicating considerably lower risk of serious health consequences than moderate or severe anaemia. Anaemia prevalence is much lower among adolescent boys, adult and older men, and even among those affected, three-fourths have only mild anaemia, said the release issued by the Union Health Ministry. SAMPADA represents one of the largest and most comprehensive nutrition surveys undertaken globally. The survey covered more than 2 lakh individuals from over 81,000 households across 183 districts in 35 States and Union Territories. More than 1.7 lakh blood samples were analysed for haemoglobin estimation across different age, sex, and physiological groups. “A major strength of SAMPADA is the use of gold standard method of venous blood sampling and automated analysers for haemoglobin estimation, providing greater accuracy and reproducibility. In a sub-sample, the survey also assessed iron status, folate, vitamin B12, together with inflammatory biomarkers C-reactive protein (CRP) and alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP) to obtain national level prevalence estimates,” the release said. Iron deficiency accounts for about half of the anaemia cases in women, adolescent girls, and children, said the report. The micronutrient assessment showed that although iron deficiency is the predominant contributor to anaemia in vulnerable population groups, it accounts for about half of the overall anaemia burden, highlighting the need to simultaneously address multiple nutritional and non-nutritional causes of anaemia, including infections, hemoglobinopathies, and inflammation related to chronic disease.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: However, the prevalence of vitamin B12 and folate deficiency was similar in both anaemic and non-anaemic individuals across population groups, indicating a limited contribution of these micronutrient deficiencies to anaemia in India.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #26 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Severe anaemia affects less than 2% of population: ICMR survey

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 09:45:22 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: SAMPADA covered more than 2 lakh individuals from over 81,000 households across 183 districts in 35 States and Union Territories

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: According to a survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), severe anaemia was observed in less than 2% of people in the majority of age groups. The Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA) 2023-2025 was released on Monday (November 23, 2026). It showed that children aged 12-59 months had 42% anaemia prevalence, adolescent girls aged 10-19 years had anaemia prevalence of 46%, adolescent boys aged 10-19 years and men aged 20–59 years had 22-23% anaemia prevalence, whereas women of reproductive age had 56% prevalence. The survey also found that mild anaemia constitutes a substantial proportion of the overall anaemia burden. “SAMPADA provides nationally representative estimates of anaemia across children, adolescents, adults, pregnant and lactating women and older adults, together with detailed information on micronutrient deficiencies to evaluate potential causes of anaemia. It is encouraging that prevalence of anaemia is lower in SAMPADA compared to previous national surveys. The comprehensive anaemia profiling in the SAMPADA survey provides an evidence base to strengthen the ongoing national efforts towards Anaemia Mukt Bharat,” said Rajiv Bahl, secretary, Department of Health Research. The report noted that about half of anaemic women, including pregnant and lactating women, adolescent girls, and children, have mild anaemia, indicating considerably lower risk of serious health consequences than moderate or severe anaemia. Anaemia prevalence is much lower among adolescent boys, adult and older men, and even among those affected, three-fourths have only mild anaemia, said the release issued by the Union Health Ministry. SAMPADA represents one of the largest and most comprehensive nutrition surveys undertaken globally. The survey covered more than 2 lakh individuals from over 81,000 households across 183 districts in 35 States and Union Territories. More than 1.7 lakh blood samples were analysed for haemoglobin estimation across different age, sex, and physiological groups. “A major strength of SAMPADA is the use of gold standard method of venous blood sampling and automated analysers for haemoglobin estimation, providing greater accuracy and reproducibility. In a sub-sample, the survey also assessed iron status, folate, vitamin B12, together with inflammatory biomarkers C-reactive protein (CRP) and alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP) to obtain national level prevalence estimates,” the release said. Iron deficiency accounts for about half of the anaemia cases in women, adolescent girls, and children, said the report. The micronutrient assessment showed that although iron deficiency is the predominant contributor to anaemia in vulnerable population groups, it accounts for about half of the overall anaemia burden, highlighting the need to simultaneously address multiple nutritional and non-nutritional causes of anaemia, including infections, hemoglobinopathies, and inflammation related to chronic disease.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: However, the prevalence of vitamin B12 and folate deficiency was similar in both anaemic and non-anaemic individuals across population groups, indicating a limited contribution of these micronutrient deficiencies to anaemia in India.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
Reproducibility (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Reproducibility' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Representative (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Representative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Severe anaemia affects less than 2% of population: ICMR survey", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. SAMPADA covered more than 2 lakh individuals from over 81,000 households across 183 districts in 35 States and Union Territories.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Severe anaemia affects less than 2% of populatio' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Severe anaemia affects less than 2% of popula' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Severe anaemia affects less than 2% of popula' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "SAMPADA covered more than 2 lakh individuals from over 81,000 households across 183 districts in 35 States and Union Territories." (Hinglish Arth: SAMPADA ने 35 राज्यों और केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों के 183 जिलों के 81,000 से अधिक घरों के 2 लाख से अधिक व्यक्तियों को कवर किया।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Severe anaemia affects less than 2% of population: ICMR survey"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. However, the prevalence of vitamin B12 and folate deficiency was similar in both anaemic and non-anaemic individuals across population groups,...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "However, the prevalence of vitamin B12 and folate deficiency was similar in both anaemic and non-anaemic individuals across population groups,..." (Hinglish Arth: हालाँकि, विटामिन बी 12 और फोलेट की कमी की व्यापकता जनसंख्या समूहों में एनीमिया और गैर-एनीमिक दोनों प्रकार के व्यक्तियों में समान थी, जो एने में इन सूक्ष्म पोषक तत्वों की कमी के सीमित योगदान का संकेत देती है।)

articles.title: Rotary Club of Madras partners with Tamil Nadu government to vaccinate 3.5 lakh girls against HPV
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The club aims to vaccinate one million children as it approaches its centenary in 2028-29

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Rotary Club of Madras (RCM) and the Tamil Nadu government have entered into a partnership to provide human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination to 3.5 lakh adolescent girls to prevent cervical cancer. The partnership, valued at approximately ₹200 crore, is among the largest public-private initiatives for HPV vaccination in India. It was acknowledged in the presence of Darez Ahamed, Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu government. High-risk HPV infections account for more than 95% of cervical cancer cases. HPV vaccination during adolescence helps prevent infections caused by high-risk HPV types and reduces the risk of cervical cancer later in life.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Bobby Krishna, president of the Rotary Club of Madras, said the partnership was part of Rotary’s efforts to work with the government on large-scale vaccination programmes. The club also aims to vaccinate one million children as it approaches its centenary in 2028-29, building on its work under the Polio Plus programme.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #27 of 30 (23 NOV)

📰 Rotary Club of Madras partners with Tamil Nadu government to vaccinate 3.5 lakh girls against HPV

📌 Published: 23 Nov 2026, 08:37:17 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The club aims to vaccinate one million children as it approaches its centenary in 2028-29

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Rotary Club of Madras (RCM) and the Tamil Nadu government have entered into a partnership to provide human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination to 3.5 lakh adolescent girls to prevent cervical cancer. The partnership, valued at approximately ₹200 crore, is among the largest public-private initiatives for HPV vaccination in India. It was acknowledged in the presence of Darez Ahamed, Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu government. High-risk HPV infections account for more than 95% of cervical cancer cases. HPV vaccination during adolescence helps prevent infections caused by high-risk HPV types and reduces the risk of cervical cancer later in life.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Bobby Krishna, president of the Rotary Club of Madras, said the partnership was part of Rotary’s efforts to work with the government on large-scale vaccination programmes. The club also aims to vaccinate one million children as it approaches its centenary in 2028-29, building on its work under the Polio Plus programme.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Karnataka needs a coherent policy on urban mobility

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While Karnataka has spent years disputing motorcycle owners’ right to carry paying passengers, Bengaluru — with the dubious distinction of having one of the world’s highest travel times per unit distance — struggles with inadequate public transport capacity and lacklustre intermediate options. The Supreme Court ruling on November 20 to dismiss Karnataka’s appeal was thus straightforward, allowing motorcycles to be registered as transport vehicles. The State has often called bike taxis unsafe, yet has not improved the prospects of safer options. Earlier this year, the Centre for Science and Environment estimated the number of buses in urban centres nationwide to be 70% short of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs benchmark and that 400 cities with populations between a lakh and 10 lakh altogether lacked organised bus services. In March, the BMTC reported a fleet of around 7,000 buses in Bengaluru, versus the 13,000 by 2025 envisaged by the Comprehensive Mobility Plan. Expanding the number of Metro stations also creates more demand for travel to and from stations, but the operating costs of the public transport corporation expected to serve that demand are not covered by the resulting increase in rail ridership. Overall, Karnataka has struggled to set up a consistent transport policy. An expert committee recommended against bike taxis in Bengaluru for first- and last-mile connectivity and in favour of better walking infrastructure and bicycle rentals in 2019, only for the State to launch the electric bike-taxi scheme in 2021, then rescind it in 2024 over safety concerns and drivers’ disputes. The market for short booked journeys is also dysfunctional. But while allowing bike taxis could temper autorickshaw fares, the State must investigate drivers’ operating costs, the difference between the paid and the received amounts, and prevent large platforms from exploiting the market. Finally, while the Union Road Transport Ministry has reported that 46.2% of all road deaths involved two-wheeler users, two-wheelers’ safety relative to autorickshaws and cabs, by the number and distance of journeys, is unclear. The State should require aggregators to report injuries and fatalities and investigate the consequences of drivers’ earnings being linked to the number of trips undertaken. The Union government’s 2025 Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines already address passenger security, fares, and insurance while allowing States to authorise privately registered motorcycles through aggregators. Karnataka should exercise this additional power. A large national programme is required to address funding for public transport, which is necessary even when it is not immediately profitable.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Developed nations must bear much of the cost of carbon emissions

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: COP31 ended in Antalya, Türkiye, with a whimper. The 190-odd countries that had convened for nearly 12 days — a close to 50-hour overshoot — failed to agree on an overarching political statement , called a cover text, that acts as a stepping stone to future, collective global action on climate change. Usually, cover texts evolve as a final synthesis of deliberations ; the COP31 leadership, helmed by Türkiye and Australia, thought it fit to push for a cover text early in the proceedings. The headline sought was a global electrification target: 35% of global final energy consumption will come from electricity by 2035, in the hope that this would reduce direct fossil fuel emissions. Ultimately, the cover text failed to pass muster because the European Union objected to the text’s lack of any explicit mention of ‘fossil fuel,’ let alone its phase-out. The COP process is arduously protracted as even a single country’s objection can stall progress. Country-blocks outside the EU, such as coalitions of the least developed countries, island nations, some South American countries — reportedly 130 countries — were also insistent on fossil fuel language. While COP 31 made some progress on old pathways, such as the Just Transition agreement, it is perplexing that the delegations could not make progress on the other big prong of negotiations: climate finance. The increase in solar panel installations and the significant shift towards battery use in grid storage and transport did not come cheap: the cost of the land required for their installation, their intermittent nature of being dependent on weather, grid upgrades all carry costs. It is global markets, imperfectly connected, but connected, that have managed to bring it to this stage over decades. India and China, major fossil emitters, with large, still indigent populations, are also leaders in total clean energy installations. Therefore it stands to reason that developed countries, which have committed to providing climate finance in recognition of their historical emissions, make good on past promises to shoulder the cost of the carbon emissions that are responsible for warming. Economic crises are a feature, and not a bug, of the interconnected financial system enveloping the world and there are, undeniably, challenges to diverting the necessary finance towards countries most vulnerable to climate change impact. However, it is no longer prudent to sweep this under the rug by scuttling experimental approaches — namely carbon capture — as inimical to the broader commitment to eschew fossil fuel. When the primary framework climate agreement was crafted three decades ago, nobody envisaged AI and the drain that data centres portended or the wars that would see the vociferous antagonists of coal immediately shore up their gas reserves. Without honest good-faith dialogue, the COP is at risk of being a sideshow: a mortal blow to multilateralism.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: climate change / Turkey / politics / Australia / electricity production and distribution / energy and resource / European Union / solar / India / China / carbon emissions / population / economy / carbon capture and sequestration / Artificial Intelligence / data management storage

1. Core Context & Background: Rohingya cannot return unless Myanmar turns democratic

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: On November 19, the International Court of Justice held that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. It is for the first time that the court has found any state responsible for the crime. The verdict, with nine votes to six, was not lightly reached. Genocide requires proof of an intent to destroy a group. In the absence of direct evidence of a plan, the court could infer that intent only if it was “the only reasonable inference” from the facts, a high bar to affix responsibility. The facts it accepted are harrowing. In 2017, in what Myanmar’s army called “clearance operations” against the insurgent Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, at least 10,000 Rohingya were killed, 1,834 raped and 392 villages destroyed in northern Rakhine State. Over 7,00,000 fled to Bangladesh. Then Army chief Min Aung Hlaing, now Myanmar’s “civilian” President, called the “Bengali problem” an “unfinished job”. Myanmar argued that it had only been fighting insurgents or at worst, driving the Rohingya out or punishing them. The court said that the army drew no distinction between fighters and civilians, had no plan to move anyone, fired on fleeing people and killed children on a scale that could not be explained as punishment. Seen alongside decades of discrimination, the evidence pointed to an intent to destroy. The incidents of 2017 were no aberration. The army drove lakhs of Rohingya into Bangladesh in 1978 and 1991-92. The junta stripped the Rohingya of citizenship in 1982 and the state branded them as “foreigners” in Arakan, disenfranchising them in 2015. While the junta’s Bamar-Buddhist vision has oppressed every minority, the Rohingya have been subjected to the most brutality. More than 1.2 million are in Bangladesh, living in dilapidated conditions, made worse due to diminished international aid. The court ordered Myanmar to allow their safe, voluntary and dignified return and to compensate them, but it has no means of enforcing its judgment. Only the UN Security Council can, but it will be subject to vetoes by Myanmar’s backers, China and Russia. On the very day of the verdict, the two joined the U.S. in Shenzhen to declare the “immunities of State officials” of “paramount importance”. Others, India among them, have courted the regime in Naypyitaw regardless, following sham elections that made the junta leader civilian President earlier this year. And Rakhine State, mired in civil war, is now mostly held by the Arakan Army which is accused of atrocities against the Rohingya. Only a truly democratic, federal, plural and peaceful Myanmar can bring the Rohingya home in safety.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: international court or tribunal / Myanmar / Rohingya crisis / crime / armed Forces / sexual assault / Bangladesh / Citizenship / welfare / United Nations / China / Russia / India / democracy

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Even a low base effect could not push India’s oil and gas sectors into growth

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The construction-related sectors seem to have seen genuine growth, a reflection of the government’s ongoing infrastructure push. The iron ore sector’s growth rate accelerated to a three-month high of 26.4% in October 2026 as compared to a growth of 8.7% in the same month last year. Steel grew at 7.3% versus 9.5% last year, and cement by 15.4% versus 5.2%. The economy’s dependence on government spending is not going to ease in the near future, and might even intensify as higher costs eat into companies’ profit margins. The core sector data once again highlighted a major reason for these higher costs — the oil and gas sectors. The crude oil sector shrank by 4.1%, its 22nd consecutive month of contraction. The natural gas sector, similarly, contracted 7.6%, a series-worst performance and the 28th straight month of contraction. A major reason behind high inflation in India is the underperformance of these two sectors and the resultant dependence on imported fuel. It is time the Petroleum Ministry candidly explains — to Parliament in December or to the public directly — why India’s fuel output has been continuously falling. If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite another. Accountability needs to be set.

1. Core Context & Background: Climate action has to be timely, with adequate resources and monitoring

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: That all was not well with the Green India Mission was clear even before its approval. After the UPA-I government announced it in 2008, the Ministry of Rural Development had objected to its financial design much before the Union Cabinet approved it in 2014. But the Environment Ministry proceeded anyway and retained largely the same arrangement when it revised the Mission in 2021. Following the Comptroller and Auditor General’s report, on November 19, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) upbraided the Ministry for the Mission’s virtual failure and for still not having issued the implementation guidelines for the revised form. The original 10-year vision was to expand forest and tree cover by 5 million hectares (mha), improve forest quality on another 5 mha, improve forest-related livelihoods for 3 million households, and sequester up to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. The outlay was ₹46,000 crore. In 2014, the Cabinet approved ₹13,000 crore for 1.4 mha each of the first two objectives by 2018, but to be supported to the tune of 81.5% by Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), National Afforestation Programme (NAP), and MGNREGS funds. In 2021-22, the Ministry folded the NAP into the Mission and, in mid-2025, unveiled a revised version with an allocation of ₹12,190 crore to improve forest cover on 25 mha by 2030, including 24 mha through other schemes. The government had thus expanded the primary target but left the Mission responsible for only 1 mha.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Together with the CAMPA, NAP, and MGNREGS funds never materialising, it is no surprise that the programmes to improve forest quality and forest cover have respectively fallen short by 91.8% and 97.5% vis-à-vis the 2014 target. The Environment Ministry had assembled a large programme around resources that it knew it could not control. Pro-climate work in practice ought to span government schemes to deliver action and justice, and the Ministry ought to have formalised the division of responsibilities and accounting system. The PAC’s new demand that the Ministry submit an implementation timetable is insufficient. From the Jal Shakti Abhiyan in 2019 to the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan in 2024, the government has often floated new programmes banking significantly on funds from existing schemes — an untenable policy when the latter also have their own obligations. And if the VB-G RAM G scheme was to also advance climate justice, the government should not have undermined the erstwhile demand-driven funding model and shifted more financial responsibility to the States. Climate action has to be timely, for which the Union government must dedicate adequate resources and proactively ensure that its initiatives are implemented.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India’s satellite supply chain is “highly dependent” on imports for critical components and the private sector’s contribution is limited to “structural assemblies” and “propulsion components” largely supplied by established public sector firms and vintage private firms, said a report by IN-SPACe, India’s regulatory-cum-promotional body for the private space sector. While pointing out the potential of India’s private space companies, the autonomous body under the Department of Space underlined the challenges ahead. Science Minister Jitendra Singh earlier this week said that India’s space economy is currently valued at nearly $9 billion and is set to increase to $40-45 billion in less than a decade, with the private sector set to grow from a a few startups “to nearly 400-500 companies in just a few years”. The Supply Chain Landscape of Satellite Manufacturing in India report, which was made public on Wednesday, says that nearly 60% of satellite costs were attributed to electronic, electrical and electromechanical components, and specialised materials, many of which are imported. India also has limited testing and certification facilities, which weakened prospects for acceptance in global markets. Many companies largely operated on a “project-based manufacturing model”, which disincentivised long-term investment in automation and production capacity, the report noted. Critical components often took a long time to procure – frequently 12-16 months – which led to project delays and hobbled responsiveness to market opportunities. There was also a shortage of trained and skilled personnel in satellite systems engineering, quality assurance, testing and qualification, besides limited private-sector research and development and technology transfer. The report was prepared by Brijesh Kumar Sol and Yudhishthir J. of IN-SPACe and “approved” by Pawan Goenka, IN-SPACe chairman.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The report isn’t a statistical survey, but paints a descriptive map of India’s satellite manufacturing supply chain.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Hyderabad must raise the share of public transport in daily travel from the current 28% to at least 40%, and eventually beyond 60%, to prevent traffic congestion from worsening, said Shashi Verma, Chief Technology Officer of Transport for London (TfL), on Wednesday.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Addressing an interactive session on Hyderabad’s traffic challenges and lessons from London’s experience at Hyderabad Metro Rail Bhavan, he called for bold policy reforms and substantial investment in public transport. The session was organised by N.V.S. Reddy, Adviser to the Telangana government on Urban Transport and Metro Rail. Mr. Verma said authorities should also consider demand-management measures to discourage excessive use of private vehicles. Both financial and non-financial measures had played an important role in managing congestion in London and other global cities, and similar approaches could be explored in India. Sharing London’s experience, he said rapid urban expansion had led to severe traffic congestion. In response, 14 separate agencies overseeing roads, railways, buses, the London Underground and suburban rail services were brought under a single authority, Transport for London. A strong mayoral governance system with extensive powers further helped improve urban mobility. He said widening roads was neither easy nor sufficient in large cities. Flyovers and other infrastructure projects could offer only limited relief, while sustainable traffic management required a robust public transport network and quality pedestrian infrastructure. Mr. Verma called for expansion of metro rail and bus services to meet future demand. More buses and wider, safer footpaths would improve first- and last-mile connectivity, make public transport more attractive and encourage people to shift away from private vehicles. He said policymakers should view urban development as a driver of prosperity and prioritise infrastructure investment. Along with metro rail expansion, cities needed affordable, efficient and cost-effective public transport options.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: HMR additional managing director B. Ajith Reddy, Secunderabad DRM R. Gopalakrishnan, Cyberabad Police Commissioner M. Ramesh and UMTA Managing Director Jeevan Babu attended the session, said a press release.
